patterns.name: SIM Swap Fraud
patterns.short_desc: Attacker duplicates your SIM to intercept OTPs and drain accounts
patterns.full_desc: The fraudster impersonates you to your telecom provider and gets a new SIM issued for your number. All incoming OTPs now go to them. They reset your UPI PIN and initiate large transfers before you notice your phone has lost signal.
how_it_happens: Fraudster collects your personal info from social media or data breaches
Calls telecom pretending to be you, reports SIM lost
New SIM issued — your phone loses signal
They receive all OTPs, reset UPI PIN, drain account
warning_signs: Your phone suddenly loses network signal
You stop receiving calls/SMS unexpectedly
You get OTP messages you didn't request
Unknown login alerts from your bank
patterns.immediate_action: Call your telecom operator immediately to verify SIM activity. Block UPI via your bank's 24x7 helpline.
patterns.prevention: Enable SIM lock with your telecom. Set a UPI transaction limit. Use a separate number for banking.

patterns.name: Fake Collect Request
patterns.short_desc: Fraudster sends a payment request disguised as money you will receive
patterns.full_desc: The most common UPI fraud. The fraudster sends a 'collect' request — you see a notification that looks like someone is sending you money. When you enter your PIN, you are actually APPROVING A PAYMENT OUT, not receiving anything.
how_it_happens: You list an item for sale or post about needing money
Fraudster contacts you as a 'buyer' or 'helper'
They send a UPI collect request instead of paying you
You enter PIN thinking you are receiving — you just sent them money
warning_signs: Someone asks you to 'approve' a payment to receive money
You are asked to enter your PIN to get a refund
The payment notification says 'Pay' not 'Receive'
patterns.immediate_action: NEVER enter your UPI PIN to receive money. You only enter PIN to SEND. If you already did, call your bank immediately to freeze the account.
patterns.prevention: Golden Rule: You only enter UPI PIN to SEND money. No exceptions. Ever.

patterns.name: Fake QR Code Scam
patterns.short_desc: Fraudster replaces legitimate QR codes or sends fake ones via WhatsApp
patterns.full_desc: Physical QR codes at shops are replaced with the fraudster's QR. Or a buyer/seller sends you a QR code claiming it is for 'verification' or 'refund'. Scanning and paying completes the fraud.
how_it_happens: Fraudster sticks their QR code over a merchant's legitimate QR
Or sends a QR via WhatsApp/SMS claiming to be a refund
Victim scans and pays, money goes to fraudster
Merchant never receives payment
warning_signs: QR code at a merchant looks tampered or is a sticker on top
Someone sends you a QR to 'receive' a refund
Recipient name after scanning is unfamiliar
patterns.immediate_action: Do not proceed with the payment. Verify recipient name. Contact the merchant directly via a known number.
patterns.prevention: Always check recipient name after scanning QR. Never trust QR codes sent via WhatsApp or SMS.

patterns.name: OTP / Vishing Fraud
patterns.short_desc: Fraudster calls as bank agent and tricks you into sharing OTP or PIN
patterns.full_desc: You receive a call from someone claiming to be from your bank, NPCI, or government. They create urgency — your account will be blocked, your KYC expired, you won a prize. They ask for your OTP or UPI PIN to 'verify' or 'process' something.
how_it_happens: You receive an urgent call from a 'bank official'
They know your name, partial account number (from data leaks)
They create panic — 'your account will be blocked in 2 hours'
They ask for OTP 'to verify your identity'
Once shared, they complete a transaction
warning_signs: Unsolicited call from 'bank' or 'NPCI'
Extreme urgency and panic creation
They ask for OTP, PIN, or full card number
They ask you to make a 'test transaction'
patterns.immediate_action: Hang up immediately. Your bank will NEVER ask for OTP or PIN. Call your bank's official number from the back of your card to verify.
patterns.prevention: No bank, NPCI, or government official ever asks for OTP or PIN. This is an absolute rule.

patterns.name: OLX / Marketplace Fraud
patterns.short_desc: Fake buyers/sellers on OLX, Facebook Marketplace, or classified sites
patterns.full_desc: As a seller, you receive a 'payment confirmation' screenshot but money never actually arrives. As a buyer, you pay advance for an item that is never delivered. Military personnel are often impersonated as buyers.
how_it_happens: You post an item for sale on OLX/social media
Buyer contacts you, agrees to price, asks for bank/UPI details
Sends a fake payment screenshot from an edited app
Pressures you to ship before you check your balance
Or asks you to pay 'delivery charges' via UPI link
warning_signs: Buyer insists on paying via UPI link instead of standard transfer
They send a payment 'confirmation' screenshot
They pressure you to ship before you check your account
The amount in your account doesn't match the screenshot
patterns.immediate_action: Always verify money has arrived in your actual bank account before shipping anything. Do not trust screenshots.
patterns.prevention: Check actual bank balance. Ship only after confirmed credit. Meet in person for high-value transactions.

patterns.name: KYC Expiry / Account Block Scam
patterns.short_desc: Fraudster claims your KYC expired and account will be blocked
patterns.full_desc: You receive an SMS or WhatsApp message claiming your bank/UPI KYC has expired and your account will be blocked within hours. You are directed to a link or asked to call a number, where they collect your credentials.
how_it_happens: SMS/WhatsApp: 'Your KYC expired. Click link or account blocked'
Link leads to a fake bank website that looks identical to real one
You enter your credentials — they now have your login
Or you are asked to send a 'verification amount' of ₹1
warning_signs: Urgency: 'Account will be blocked in 24 hours'
Link in SMS/WhatsApp to complete KYC
Asked to make a ₹1 test payment
Asked to download an app to complete KYC
patterns.immediate_action: Do not click any link. KYC is never done via UPI payment or SMS links. Visit your bank branch directly.
patterns.prevention: KYC is done in-person at a bank branch or through the bank's official verified app only.

patterns.name: Advance Fee / Lottery Fraud
patterns.short_desc: Promise of large reward requires a small 'processing fee' first
patterns.full_desc: You are told you have won a lottery, a job, a loan, or a government scheme. To claim it, you must first pay a small 'processing fee', 'GST', 'registration', or 'security deposit'. The fee is collected, the reward never materialises.
how_it_happens: Message: 'You won ₹50 lakh in KBC lottery!'
Or: 'Easy work from home, earn ₹50,000/month, pay ₹500 registration'
Or: 'Your loan approved, pay 2% processing fee first'
Small payment made, fraudster disappears or asks for more
warning_signs: Unsolicited win or offer that seems too good
Any upfront payment required to receive a benefit
Payment via UPI to an unknown individual (not a company)
Urgency: 'Offer expires in 2 hours'
patterns.immediate_action: Stop all payments. Legitimate lotteries, employers, and lenders never ask for upfront fees.
patterns.prevention: If you have to pay to receive money, it is always fraud. No exceptions.

patterns.name: Remote Access / Screen Share Fraud
patterns.short_desc: Fraudster installs AnyDesk/TeamViewer and controls your phone directly
patterns.full_desc: Fraudster calls as 'bank tech support' and convinces you to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer, or QuickSupport. Once installed, they have full control of your phone — they can see your OTPs, open your banking apps, and initiate transactions while you watch.
how_it_happens: Call from 'tech support' about a problem with your account/phone
They ask you to install AnyDesk or similar app
You share the access code — they now control your screen
They open your UPI app, send money to multiple accounts
They may ask you to open your banking app 'to fix the issue'
warning_signs: Any request to install AnyDesk, TeamViewer, QuickSupport
Request to share your screen
Being asked to open your banking app while on a call
Transactions you did not initiate appearing on screen
patterns.immediate_action: IMMEDIATELY uninstall AnyDesk/TeamViewer. Turn off mobile data/WiFi. Call bank helpline 1930 to freeze account. File complaint at cybercrime.gov.in.
patterns.prevention: No legitimate bank or tech support ever asks you to install remote access software. Hang up.
